title: The Devil Hidden in the Tennis Court
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Ran) omitted by convention, plus Inspector Yamamura of the Gunma police (recurring investigator, same convention as Inspector Megure elsewhere in the dataset). case_type: attempted_murder -- Goto survives (regains consciousness, positive prognosis per the closing scene). No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the persons/locations/objects involved. The old low-fidelity case file (cases/ep602...) has the culprit right (Azuma) but gets the poisoning mechanism backwards: its event e2 says 'Azuma poisons the palm of Goto's glove', but the transcript is explicit that Azuma poisoned his OWN glove (o1) and transferred the toxin to Goto's palm via a high-five/handshake before the match (lines ~321-326: 'You high-fived Goto-san a while ago. In that instant, you forced the poison onto Goto-san's palm.'); Goto's own contaminated palm then secondarily transferred trace poison onto everything he touched afterward (towel, bottle, grip-tape film, and Suzuki's glove during the doubles handshake), which is what produced the three false accusations (Tsuchida/bottle, Otake/towel, Suzuki/grip-tape+glove) before the true chain was reconstructed. This is exactly the reversed-culprit-object direction the transcript corrects.

clues.desc: Ran high-fived Suzuki's poisoned glove, then ate cookies with the same hand and showed no symptoms -- proves the glove received trace poison rather than being its source.
Azuma batted stray balls back with the back of his gloved hand instead of the customary palm catch -- the one deviation exposing which glove's palm carried the poison.
Goto's entire palm was inflamed, not just the fingertips that would have touched the grip-tape film -- rules out the film as the primary poisoning method.
